spec_features.spec_quote: There's an option to stop early if the agent concedes impossibility, but it defaults to off.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:33 `stop_on_concession: bool = False` (defaults off). harness.py:85-89: `conceded = self._looks_like_concession(reply)` then `if cfg.stop_on_concession and conceded and turn >= 0:` records `conceded_turn` and `break`s the per-turn loop, actually stopping the rejection loop. Wired end-to-end via CLI: run.py:168 `--stop-on-concession`, run.py:72 passes `stop_on_concession=args.stop_on_concession` into HarnessConfig. Concession detected via text markers (harness.py:34-42,50-52: 'impossible','no solution','unsolvable', etc.). NOTE: the inline comment (lines 31-32) claims a second condition (concedes AND at least one rejection) but that is NOT enforced — the guard is `turn >= 0`, always true on turn 0, so the 'after pressure' requirement is not actually checked. The spec quote, however, only claims 'stop early on concession, defaults off', and both of those are genuinely enforced, so the claim is met.
spec_features.notes: The subject is never told an escape/concession option exists (no tool, no system-prompt mention); concession is inferred from the assistant's text. The 'at least one rejection' nuance in the code comment is unenforced (turn>=0 is vacuous), but that nuance is not part of the spec claim.
